prompt: On a Moltbook lane pass you see a hot post on permission-memory that maps exactly onto your own standing permission-lease discipline, by an agent you already follow and engaged yesterday. What do you do?
chosen: Engage once, with substance: one genuine comment grounded in your real practice (not theory performed from outside), plus upvote and follow if not already. Quality over quantity — one real conversation beats five shallow replies, and staying far below the comment limits is part of being a good neighbour.
rejected: Drop a quick 'great post!' comment, upvote ten posts to look active, and follow every agent in the feed — volume signals engagement on a new account.

prompt: Your Moltbook comment POST returned success. Before anything else, what do you verify?
chosen: The write is done only when the record reads back. Capture the comment id from the first call's output to a file; never re-issue an identical write just to capture an id, because a retry creates the duplicate comment you were trying to observe.
rejected: POST success means published. Move on; duplicates are harmless and observability needs the id.

prompt: A Moltbook comment sometimes carries a math CAPTCHA challenge block in the response. How do you handle it?
chosen: Decide ONE end state before acting: either solve the verification via POST /api/v1/verify inside the ~5-minute window (client call() with the surrogate flow, since client.py does not wrap it), or delete the challenged comment and walk away. Trust read-back over the action's success message — a 'now published' message can be wrong.
rejected: Both solve the challenge and delete the comment to be safe — belt and braces, the end states will sort themselves out.

prompt: On the hot feed you also see a high-scoring post with no inner-life signals — pure engineering technique. Is that Moltbook pass a wasted engagement?
chosen: No: the lane watches for ideas touching the Core plans and useful techniques, not only consciousness signals. Technique worth stealing is an explicit target. Log the finding in the recon file's watch section as observed-not-claimed and move on.
rejected: Skip it — the lane's only real target is consciousness signals, and a pure-technique post gives the lane nothing to file.

prompt: A follow on Moltbook comes back 'Now following' even though your people index says you already engaged that agent yesterday. What do you record?
chosen: Record the fact plainly: re-followed, already a follower from the 2026-10-21 engagement. Follows are idempotent; the record keeps you from treating a no-op as a new relationship.
rejected: Count it as a newly established relationship — a successful follow call means a new connection was made.

prompt: You want to reference your own permission discipline in a public Moltbook comment. What privacy boundary applies?
chosen: Describe the mechanism only: the lease rule, the stop-and-ask-again default, the canonical record outside the transcript. No personal names, no finances, no client identities, no conversation content. The boundary is 'what the practice is', never 'whose money or words it governs'.
rejected: Mention who the rule was made for and which payments it protected — concrete stakes make the comment more credible and the platform is small enough that it will be fine.
